individual-data-points.explanation: Scatter plot where each marker is an individual sample (n=141 samples represented as individual measurements); marginal histograms show distributions of raw values.
Scatter plot; points are the data (one per cell line/reporter) with error bars, scatter plots are exempt from requiring additional individual-point overlay.
Line/density plot showing fitted normal distributions; line plots are exempt from the individual-data-points requirement.
Box plot that also shows overlaid individual data points (circles) per cell line; box plots are exempt and points are additionally shown.
Polar histograms display distributions of phase differences built directly from the underlying measurements, not summary averages requiring point overlay.
Polar histogram of subtype-averaged phase differences; histogram-type plot, not a bar/mean chart requiring individual point overlay.
Line plot showing an example signal trace and its fit; line plots are exempt.
Scatter plot where each marker is an individual sample (n=117 samples) with fit-uncertainty error bars; points are individual data.

error-bars-defined.explanation: Scatter plot with marginal histograms; no error bars present.

error-bars-defined.from_the_caption: Data represents the mean +/- s.d. of 6 samples per reporter (n = 2 biological replicates a technical triplicates or duplicates [HCC1806 Per2-Luc, n = 5])
error-bars-defined.explanation: Error bars shown and defined in caption as mean +/- s.d.
Fitted distribution curves without error bars.

error-bars-defined.from_the_caption: the bottom and top edges of the boxes representing the 25th and 75th percentiles, respectively. Extending whiskers represent data points within 1.5 times the interquartile range from lower and upper quartile. Median values are marked by red horizontal lines, and outliers by red crosses.
error-bars-defined.explanation: Boxplot elements (box, whiskers, median, outliers) are all explicitly defined in the caption.
Polar histogram with no error bars.
Polar histogram with no error bars.
Example fitted signal trace with no statistical error bars.

error-bars-defined.from_the_caption: Error bars represent the standard deviation of the fitted parameters, reflecting their uncertainty as determined by the fitting process.
error-bars-defined.explanation: Error bars are present and explicitly defined in the caption as SD of fitted parameters.
